summary: Multiplexed streaming 502s during mid-morning tenant burst linked to ephemeral-worker shed
description:
Issue summary: Between 09:20 and 10:05 PDT on 2026-03-13 several customers observed intermittent 502 responses on multiplexed streaming endpoints. The errors coincided with a mid-morning tenant burst from a few heavy tenants on Dedicated pools. Impact: streaming sessions saw partial responses followed by 502s; reconnect loops caused visible degradation for ScribeAI (dedicated tenant) and a small set of other tenants. Not a global outage but high error-rate window for affected tenants.

Observed behavior: API gateway returned 502s with upstream read timeout/connection reset. Upstream runtime pods reported short-lived OOM restarts and voluntary eviction of ephemeral worker threads. Autoscaler logs show a rapid shed of ephemeral workers while persistent workers remained. Traffic pattern: long-lived multiplexed HTTP/2 streams with periodic large token bursts (embedding + generation mix).
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use multiplexed streaming client to open 100 concurrent HTTP/2 streams to a single tenant in prod us-west 2)
2) Send alternating large embedding batches (~1k tokens) and generation requests (seq len 1k) from multiple logical clients 3)
3) Observe increased API gateway 502s and upstream runtime restarts when concurrency crosses ~80 streams
logs: apigw: 2026-03-13T09:34:12Z - 502 upstream read timeout - upstream=10.20.14.22:8080 request_id=abcd-1234
runtime: 2026-03-13T09:34:13Z - watchdog: ephemeral_worker_evicted id=0x7f4ca mem_pressure=0.78 restarts=3
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: apigw timeouts due to slow down at runtime when many long-stream sessions hold KV cache leading to backpressure.
Found correlation between ephemeral worker eviction events and peak 502 rate (cross-correlation r=0.82).
Heap/allocator traces show repeated small allocations from streaming multiplex code path causing increased GC pauses on ephemeral workers, triggering autoscaler memory heuristics.

Difference vs past incidents: persistent workers continued serving, but multiplexed streams rely on ephemeral workers for parsing/IO; eviction caused half-open sockets and apigw considered upstream unhealthy leading to immediate 502s.
Traffic replay from staging reproduced socket half-open pattern when ephemeral worker pool dropped below concurrency threshold.
mitigation: 1) Immediate: increased ephemeral worker target from 4 -> 16 for affected Dedicated pools (manual override) to absorb burst
2) Short-term: raised apigw upstream read timeout from 10s -> 20s for multiplexed route to reduce premature 502s (temporary config),
3) Customer guidance: advised ScribeAI to enable request-level retry with jitter and to spread large embedding batches across time windows
resolution: Root cause: aggressive ephemeral-worker shedding during memory-pressure detection combined with long-lived multiplexed streams holding socket resources produced half-open upstream connections; apigw treated these as unhealthy upstreams and returned 502s. Fixes: reverted the aggressive shed heuristic in autoscaler and added a minimum ephemeral_worker floor for multiplexed-route pools (runtime change merged). Deployed autoscaler patch (PR #2874) 2026-03-13 23:15 UTC and adjusted prod configs; observed error rates fall to baseline within one hour after scale changes. Postmortem and follow-ups created.
postmortem_followups: 1) Add unit/regression tests for multiplexed stream behavior under ephemeral-worker eviction
2) Tweak memory heuristic to consider stream-depth and socket-hold-time before shedding ephemeral workers
3) Add dashboard alert for ephemeral_worker_evicted spikes tied to apigw 502s
4) Update customer-facing runbook for tenants using multiplexed streaming (recommend batching windows and retry guidance)
